A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the presence of a KDEL ER-retaining signal in the carboxy-terminus of the Autographacalifornica nucleopolyhedral virus chitinase is not essential for enzyme activity, but is required for the retention of the enzyme within the ER.

the KDEL motif is not essential for chitinase activity or secretion, and that its retention within the ER is likely to be a consequence of a requirement to maintain the enzyme at a specific intracellular location.

the chitinase of Autographa calificonica nucleopolyhedroviruses (AcMNPVs) is not a secreted protein, but is a resident ER protein that is released into the extracellular environment by terminal cell lysis.
The main takeaway from our work is that
chitinase is not an essential gene for viral replication and dissemination in the insect host, but that its activity is important for efficient liquefaction of the host cadaver.

the KDEL motif is not essential for chitinase activity or for the liquefying properties of the virus, and that a significant proportion of this chitinase can be secreted into the medium prior to cell lyses.

chitinase can be released into the extracellular environment of insect cells by mutation of the ER retention signal and that this may have important implications for the use of chitinase in baculovirus-based biocontrol agents.
